# Monster Battle 9001: Voice Script

<!-- Generated by tools/audio/voice/build.sh (mbvoice/scriptdoc.py) from shared/src/defs/voiceLines.json. Edit the data file, not this page. -->

Every spoken line in the game, grouped by the moment that triggers it. There are 221 lines for 34 moments ("cues").

This page is the readable copy for review. The copy the game and the voice generator actually use is the script data file `shared/src/defs/voiceLines.json`. This page is written again from that file every time the voices are built, so the two cannot drift apart.

## How it works

- The game announces a **cue** when something happens (a volley is fired, a building falls). Each cue has several alternative lines, and the game plays one of them, never the one it played last time, so the chatter does not repeat itself too quickly.
- Every line is also shown as a subtitle. Subtitles and names are the only text in the game, so every line is short enough to read at a glance: twelve words at most (20 for the hearing on the end screen).
- Each side hears its own show. **The human squads hear military radio** (129 lines). **The kaiju player hears a live Channel 9 news broadcast about its own rampage** (86 lines). The hearing on the end screen is heard by everyone (6 lines).
- Line names follow one pattern: `v_`, the cue name with dots turned into underscores, then a number. The same name is used for the sound file. New lines get the next free number, so the numbers of one cue are not sorted by side.

## The cast

| Voice | Heard by | Who they are | How they talk | Lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Overlord** | Humans | Command. Stern and unhurried. | Gives orders, never explains twice. Knows exactly how many forms a stray shot costs. | 50 |
| **Granite** | Humans | Squad callsign. The veteran. | Says as little as possible. Nothing surprises Granite, including this. | 26 |
| **Beacon** | Humans | Squad callsign. By the book. | Full sentences, cites the manual, reports everything that must be reported, and is already filling in the form. | 26 |
| **Tempest** | Humans | Squad callsign. Has taken the creature personally. | Speaks in vows and keeps count. Never shouts. | 27 |
| **Anchor** | Kaiju | The Channel 9 news anchor. | Total professional calm. Covers the end of the city the way other anchors cover traffic. | 86 |
| **Chair** | Everyone | Chair of the committee hearing after the match. | Bureaucratic gravity. Summarizes the outcome and moves to the paperwork. | 6 |

The game has four human squads. Three of them have a voice of their own (Granite, Beacon and Tempest). When a cue is about one squad (its volley, its losses, what it has spotted, the building it hit), the game uses only that squad's own lines; it never puts one squad's words in another squad's mouth. The fourth squad, Anvil, has no voice of its own: Overlord speaks for it. That is why each of the four radio voices needs several lines of its own for those cues, and why the table of line counts at the end of this page shows them per voice.

## Tone rules

- Flight-combat radio melodrama, deadly serious. The world is absurd and nobody in it notices.
- Nobody winks and nobody jokes. The comedy is the gravity.
- A shot that misses the creature and hits the city should make its commander feel the paperwork coming.
- Nothing mean-spirited. No real people, places, brands or existing monsters.

## Rules for writing new lines

Anyone adding or changing lines should keep to these, because the voices are generated by simple offline speech synthesizers and checked by speech recognition. The build checks the rules marked (checked) and refuses to run when one is broken.

- Twelve words or fewer; 20 for the hearing (checked).
- Plain words. Numbers written out ("ten seconds", "Channel Nine"). No abbreviations, no contractions, and no punctuation except periods and commas (checked).
- Avoid words that can be said two ways, because a synthesizer has to guess: live, lead, read, close, wind, record, present, object, minute as in tiny (checked against a longer list).
- Never name the creature, the city or a landmark. The humans say "the target" or "it"; the anchor says "the creature". That way every line works for all four kaiju and any map.
- Avoid words that only fit one faction ("tanks", "shells", "artillery"). Say "units", "shots", "a strike".
- Lines for a moment anyone could have caused (a building falling) must not say who caused it.
- A line must stay true every time it plays. Nothing is "new" or "the first" in a line that can come round again a minute later.
- When a line announces a short window, put the order first and keep it short. The humans' lines for a nerve break and for the signature attack must take 2.5 seconds or less as built (checked): about five words for Overlord, who speaks slowly, and six for the squads.
- A squad never announces its own destruction: "squad wiped out" belongs to Overlord (checked).
- Variety is counted per voice, not per cue (checked): `volley.ready` 3, `volley.fired` 3, `crossfire` 2, `nerve.break` 2, `unit.lost` 2, `kaiju.spotted` 2, `collateral.human` 2 lines for each of Overlord, Granite, Beacon and Tempest.
- Try the wording before it goes in: `tools/audio/voice/tryline.py <Voice> "candidate" ..` speaks candidates with that voice and its radio and prints how long they are and what the speech recognizer hears. Short sentences made of long, common words survive the radio best. Words that did not survive it: "staggered", "hit it", "reloading", "hurt" in Tempest's accent, and a callsign at the start of a line.

## The script

Cues marked frequent happen many times a match and have at least four alternatives for each side. Cues marked repeating come round about once a minute and have at least three. Lengths are those of the finished sound files, in seconds.

### Before the match

#### Briefing (`match.briefing`)

On the briefing screen before the match, which lasts ten seconds. This is the one cue that is not a set of alternatives: the three lines for your side play one after another, in the numbered order, so together they must take less than ten seconds.

| `v_match_briefing_3` | Overlord | Kill it. Misses count against us. | 2.8 |

#### Nerve breaks (`nerve.break`, frequent)

The creature's nerve breaks. It staggers for five seconds and its glowing weak point opens. The humans' lines are orders for those five seconds, so they are the shortest in the script: the order comes first and the whole line takes two and a half seconds at most.

#### Signature attack (`kaiju.special`, repeating)

## How the script was checked

- Every line is checked by the build (`tools/audio/voice/mbvoice/scriptcheck.py`): valid data, unique names, every cue covered for both sides, word limits, only letters, periods and commas, no words that can be said two ways, every word present in the pronunciation dictionary the speech tools use, and enough lines per voice.
- Word counts: ordinary lines run from 2 to 12 words, 8.8 on average. Hearing lines run from 15 to 17 words.
- Speaking time of the finished files, radio clicks and all: an ordinary line takes 3.4 seconds on average and 5.1 at most; a hearing line takes 6.6 to 8.6 seconds, including the ring of the room.
- The briefing for the humans takes 9.0 seconds of speech in a 10 second briefing (limit 9.2, which leaves room for the short gaps between the lines).
- The briefing for the kaiju player takes 8.6 seconds of speech in a 10 second briefing (limit 9.2, which leaves room for the short gaps between the lines).
- The humans' lines for `nerve.break` take 2.1 to 2.5 seconds (limit 2.5).
- The humans' lines for `kaiju.special` take 2.0 to 2.3 seconds (limit 2.5).
- Every finished line is played back to a speech recognizer (details in `docs/audio/VOICE.md`, section 4). Over the whole script it gets 7.5 words in a hundred wrong; a person hears far better than it does. The lines it garbled worst were reworded.
- Known weak spot: the word "volley" and the callsigns "Granite" and "Beacon" are often misheard by the speech recognizer (as "valley", "granted", "he can" and similar). They are clear to a person, and the subtitle is always there, but the two-word line "Volley away." scores badly in machine checks for that reason.
